title: Frame.io Pricing 2026: Plans, Storage Limits, Real Costs
summary: Frame.io pricing tiers are broken down here so you can select the subscription that best fits your team's storage needs and project volume.
body_markdown:
## Frame.io Pricing and Plan Structure


Target User Plan Monthly Price per Seat Key Value Prop


Solo Freelancers Free $0 Basic feedback for single-track projects


Boutique Creators Pro $15 Unlimited projects for independent professionals


Production Agencies Team $25 Custom-branded shares for a professional client-facing look


Media Conglomerates Enterprise Custom Single Sign-On (SSO) and audit logs


### Which frame.io plan fits you?


When a solo editor needs simple client approval on a single project, they fit the Free Plan.


This tier costs $0 but limits active storage, which restricts the volume of files you can access without upgrading, forcing you to choose between paying or deleting your work.


$15 per seat is the entry point for independent creators managing multiple clients simultaneously on the Pro Plan. They lack team-wide asset sharing, so they must manually duplicate files to collaborate with others.


Boutique agencies with more than 5 collaborators must use the Team Plan at $25 per seat. This is the lowest tier offering private workspaces, so sensitive client projects remain siloed.


Large-scale studios requiring network isolation and legal-grade security must move to Enterprise. seat minimums typically start at 25 users, forcing smaller firms to pay for unused capacity to access high-level compliance features, so smaller teams are effectively subsidizing features they do not need.


### Frame.io free plan limits for solo reviewers


The Free Plan is a lightweight entry point for individuals who need to share a single link with a client for time-stamped feedback.


A single 4K master file will likely exhaust the limit and block further uploads. Because it lacks version stacking, users can't compare iterations side-by-side.


### The Pro Plan: For growing creators ($15/user)


Professional freelancers who juggle an unlimited number of projects use the Pro Plan. At $15 per seat, it unlocks versioning tools, so teams gain the ability to track file iterations without manual naming conventions.


An editor can stack "Edit V1" and "Edit V2" to show a client exactly how the team addressed a specific note. "Team Folders" are not supported on this plan; every asset uploaded is visible to anyone invited to that project.


### The Team Plan: For collaborative studios ($25/user)


The Team Plan introduces the first level of administrative control required for studios where multiple editors work on the same account.


The $25 per seat price point includes custom-branded presentation pages, allowing you to maintain a professional client-facing aesthetic without additional software, so you can streamline your workflow into a single subscription.


Clients see the agency's logo rather than the vendor's during the review process. This tier prices per single user, letting a studio add up to 15 paid seats as needed, with no seat floor enforced regardless of staff count.


### Frame.io Enterprise plan for high-security media orgs


The Enterprise Plan is the only tier with the security infrastructure required by major film studios and corporate legal departments. It includes Single Sign-On (SSO) integration.


An IT manager can revoke access to the entire suite of assets instantly when an employee leaves the company. It also has Watermark ID, which burns the viewer's identity into the video stream to prevent unauthorized leaks.
